back_translation: When Pashhur the priest, son of Immer, who was the chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things,
Pashhur then beat Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, which is at the house of the LORD.
The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, The LORD does not call you Pashhur, but calls you Magor-missabib.

For thus says the LORD: Behold, I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends; they will fall by the sword of their enemies before your very eyes, and I will hand over all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, who will carry them away to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
I will give all the wealth of this city—its produce, its valuables, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah—into the hand of their enemies; they will plunder, seize, and carry it off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, together with all who live in your house, will go into captivity; you will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied falsely.
O LORD, you persuaded me, and I was persuaded; you were stronger than I and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
For whenever I speak, I must cry out, proclaiming, Violence and destruction! For the word of the LORD has become to me a reproach and a derision all day long.
But if I say, I will not mention Him, nor speak in His name any longer, that word becomes like a burning fire in my heart, shut up in my bones; I am weary of holding it in and cannot endure it.

For I have heard the whispering of many, Terror is on every side! Report him; let us report him! All my close friends watch for me to stumble: Perhaps he will be enticed, then we will overcome him and take our revenge on him.

But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. They will be utterly ashamed because they did not succeed—an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
O LORD of Hosts, who tests the righteous, who examines the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For He rescues the life of the needy from the hand of the wicked.
May the day on which I was born be cursed; the day my mother bore me, let it not be blessed.
May the man who brought the news to my father be cursed—the one who said, You have a son, making my father very glad.
May that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without changing his mind; may he hear an outcry in the morning and a battle cry at noon,
because he did not kill me from the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave, and her womb pregnant forever.
Why did I have to come out of the womb, to see only trouble and sorrow, and for my days to end in shame?
